rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that Arabic permits commanding someone to do good with either a bi-marked complement or a direct object; an unnamed poet witnesses the direct construction.
rows.anchor: أمرت زيدا بالخير وأمرت زيدا الخير قال الشاعر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He alternatively reads Moses as choosing the respected people among his nation for the rendezvous; قومه names the intended group generically, and سبعين رجلا is apposition, avoiding the other explanations' strained parsing.
rows.anchor: وعندي فيه وجه آخر وهو أن يكون التقدير : واختار موسى قومه لميقاتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Moses selected twelve tribes, six from each, totaling seventy-two; two stayed after a dispute when Moses promised them the same reward, and Caleb and Joshua remained.
rows.anchor: ذكروا أن موسى عليه السلام اختار من قومه اثني عشر سبطا من كل سبط ستة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Moses found only sixty elders, so God directed him to choose ten young men who became elders; he ordered fasting, purification, and clean clothes before the rendezvous.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه لم يجد إلا ستين شيخا ، فأوحى الله إليه أن يختار من الشبان عشرة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The first interpretation identifies this as the rendezvous for speech and the request to see God: the seventy went to Sinai, heard God address Moses, then requested a vision and were struck by the thunderbolt called the quake here.
rows.anchor: إنه عليه السلام خرج بهؤلاء السبعين إلى طور سيناء

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: A second interpretation makes this a different rendezvous: the seventy did not worship the calf, but failed to separate themselves from its worshippers.
rows.anchor: أن هؤلاء السبعين وإن كانوا ما عبدوا العجل إلا أنهم ما فارقوا عبدة العجل

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the seventy did too little to forbid worship of the calf.
rows.anchor: أنهم ما بالغوا في النهي عن عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: A further explanation says they asked God for a privilege never given before or after, and God's rejection of that request brought the quake.
rows.anchor: لما خرجوا إلى الميقات ليتوبوا دعوا ربهم وقالوا أعطنا ما لم تعطه أحدا قبلنا

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: They argue from narrative order: the speech and vision story is followed by the calf story and then this account, so returning to the earlier episode after completing another would disrupt eloquent arrangement.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الحال يقتضي أن تكون هذه القصة مغايرة للقصة المتقدمة

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: They infer a different episode from Moses saying the foolish people did what caused the punishment, rather than saying what they said; the offense was calf worship, not asking for a vision.
rows.anchor: فلما لم يقل موسى كذلك بل قال : { أتهلكنا بما فعل السفهاء منا }

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: They distinguish the episodes because Moses alone became unconscious and the mountain was crushed at the vision rendezvous, whereas this passage says only the people quaked.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن القوم أخذتهم الرجفة ، ولم يذكر أن موسى عليه السلام أخذته الرجفة

rows.speaker: القائلون بأن هذا الميقات هو ميقات الكلام وطلب الرؤية
rows.claim: The opposing view identifies the rendezvous with the vision episode because the earlier verse uses the same phrase, our appointed time.
rows.anchor: إنه تعالى قال في الآية الأولى : { ولما جاء موسى لميقاتنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the same-rendezvous argument weak and says the arguments favoring the speech-and-vision interpretation are stronger.
rows.anchor: وجوابه : أن هذا الدليل ضعيف ، ولا شك أن الوجوه المذكورة في تقوية القول الأول أقوى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports a third setting: Aaron died while resting at a mountain slope; Israelites accused Moses of killing him, so Moses brought seventy men, God revived Aaron to deny the charge, and the quake then struck them.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال : إن موسى وهرون عليهما السلام انطلقا إلى سفح جبل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the quake killed the seventy and God revived them; Moses feared Israel would accuse him of killing its best men and distrust him, so he wished they had died publicly before the journey.
rows.anchor: قال السدي : قال موسى يا رب كيف أرجع إلى بني إسرائيل وقد أهلكت خيارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says the quake did not kill them: terror made them shake so violently their joints nearly separated and backs nearly broke; Moses feared death, wept and prayed, and God lifted it.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الرجفة ما كانت موتا ، ولكن القوم لما رأوا تلك الحالة المهيبة أخذتهم الرعدة

rows.speaker: أهل العلم
rows.claim: Scholars say Moses cannot mean that God might punish people for others' sins; one reading takes his question as rhetorical denial, meaning God will not do so.
rows.anchor: إنه لا يجوز أن يظن موسى عليه السلام أن الله تعالى يهلك قوما بذنوب غيرهم

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad reads Moses' question as a plea for compassion: do not destroy us.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : هو استفهام استعطاف ، أي لا تهلكنا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi takes the pronoun hiya to refer to the trial: foolish people were led astray by it while others were preserved in truth, as the following clause makes explicit.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : الكناية في قوله : { هى }

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi calls the verse an evident proof against the Qadariyya, leaving them no excuse.
rows.anchor: ثم قال الواحدي : وهذه الآية من الحجج الظاهرة على القدرية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites deny that the verse supports determinism: it does not say God misleads servants from religion, and the quake itself cannot mislead, so the wording needs interpretation.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : لا تعلق للجبرية بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains the trial as God's test and demanding obligation, since the people were required to endure the quake.
rows.anchor: فأما قوله : { إن هى إلا فتنتك } فالمعنى : امتحانك وشدة تعبدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the trial guides a person to paradise if he believes and remains faithful, while God punishes one who disbelieves or fails to persevere in faith.
rows.anchor: تهدي بهذا الامتحان إلى الجنة والثواب بشرط أن يؤمن ذلك المكلف ويبقى على الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes misguidance as destruction: God destroys whom He wills through the quake and diverts it from whom He wills.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالإضلال الإهلاك ، والتقدير : تهلك من تشاء بهذه الرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation says the test is a cause of the guidance or misguidance that follows, so both may be attributed to God.
rows.anchor: لما كان هذا الامتحان كالسبب في هداية من اهتدى ، وضلال من ضل ، جاز أن يضافا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that faith and disbelief are equally possible unless a motive favors one, and God creates that motive; once it exists, the act follows, so guidance and misguidance are from God.
rows.anchor: أن القدرة الصالحة للإيمان والكفر لا يترجح تأثيرها في أحد الطرفين على تأثيرها في الطرف الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people acted solely by their own choice and aim, all rational people would choose faith, truth, and sincerity; since they do not, their outcomes are from God.
rows.anchor: أن أحدا من العقلاء لا يريد إلا الإيمان والحق والصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that self-created guidance is circular: choosing the true belief requires already knowing which belief is true, so the ability to create it would depend on that belief already existing.
rows.anchor: امتنع أن يخص أحد الاعتقادين بالتحصيل والتكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads You are our protector as exclusive: God alone protects, helps, and guides them, completing the preceding claim that He guides and misguides.
rows.anchor: يفيد الحصر ، ومعناه أنه لا ولي لنا ولا ناصر ولا هادي إلا أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks forgiveness because saying the trial is wholly God's act was a grave boldness, and asks God to overlook it.
rows.anchor: المراد منه أن إقدامه على قوله : { إن هى إلا فتنتك } جراءة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best forgiver because other beings forgive for praise, reward, or relief from inner aversion, while God forgives solely through grace and generosity.
rows.anchor: أما أنت فتغفر ذنوب عبادك لا لطلب عوض وغرض ، بل لمحض الفضل والكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This continues Moses' prayer at the quake. Since a protector removes harm and brings benefit, he first asks forgiveness and mercy, then asks for good in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: هذا من بقية دعاء موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم عند مشاهدة الرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says write for us means ordain or make binding for us; asking for good in both worlds parallels the believers' prayer in 2:201.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { واكتب } أي وجب لنا والكتابة تذكر بمعنى الإيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guardianship gives a reason to ask for benefits, displaying His grace and divinity; the servants' repentance, humility, and submission give a second reason.
rows.anchor: كونه تعالى وليا للعبد يناسب أن يطلب العبد منه دفع المضار وتحصيل المنافع

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators explain hudna ilayka as we repented and returned to You; al-Layth says al-hawd means repentance.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : { هدنا } أي تبنا ورجعنا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer rests on two grounds: God's lordly might and guardianship, and the servants' lowly state as repentant, submissive worshippers.
rows.anchor: عهد عزة الربوبية . والثاني : عهد ذلة العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says He punishes whom He wills without anyone's objection, because all belongs to Him and no one may object to an owner's disposal of exclusive property.
rows.anchor: إني أعذب من أشاء وليس لأحد علي اعتراض لأن الكل ملكي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads man asaa, from wrongdoing; al-Shafi'i preferred this reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن { من * أساء } من الإساءة ، واختار الشافعي هذه القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God's mercy encompasses everyone in this world but is reserved for believers in the afterlife, as the following conditions specify.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد من قوله : { ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says existence itself is good, so every existent has received at least the mercy of being brought into existence.
rows.anchor: قيل : الوجود خير من العدم ، وعلى هذا التقدير فلا موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another argument says good is desired intrinsically and evil only incidentally; what is intrinsic outweighs what is incidental, so mercy prevails.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخير مطلوب بالذات ، والشر مطلوب بالعرض

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites define mercy as willing good: every living being is created for mercy, pleasure, and good, and pains are offset by abundant compensations that are also divine mercy.
rows.anchor: وقال المعتزلة : الرحمة عبارة عن إرادة الخير

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school says the universal wording is intended specifically, as in the statement that Solomon was given everything.
rows.anchor: وقال أصحابنا قوله : { ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء } من العام الذي أريد به الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi classifies God's commands into prohibitions and required actions; the prohibitions require avoidance and are signaled by the description of those who are mindful.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن جميع تكاليف الله محصورة في نوعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among positive duties, the duty involving a person's wealth is zakat, signaled by the phrase about giving zakat.
rows.anchor: أما القسم الأول : فهو الزكاة وإليه الإشارة بقوله : { ويؤتون الزكواة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duties involving the person include knowledge and action: knowledge is recognition, while action includes verbal confession and bodily practice such as prayer; belief in God's signs points to this whole group.
rows.anchor: وأما القسم الثاني : فيدخل فيه ما يجب على الإنسان علما وعملا أما العلم فالمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi compares this summary of obligations with the opening of al-Baqara, which joins belief, prayer, and spending.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى في أول سورة البقرة : { هدى للمتقين * الذين يؤمنون بالغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses' story, Razi presents the covenant passage as establishing the proof against all morally responsible people.
rows.anchor: لما شرح قصة موسى عليه السلام مع توابعها على أقصى الوجوه ذكر في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Through Muslim ibn Yasar, Umar reports asking the Prophet about the verse: God extracted Adam's descendants, assigning some to paradise and its deeds and others to hell and its deeds; each is enabled in life for the destiny assigned.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عنها فقال : ( إن الله سبحانه وتعالى خلق آدم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God passed His hand over Adam's back, and every soul of his descendants through the end of time fell from it.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لما خلق الله آدم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God drew dustlike descendants from Adam, elicited their testimony; the white were destined for paradise by mercy and the black for hell, then all were returned to Adam's loins.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل : ( إن الله مسح صفحة ظهر آدم سوداء كهيئة الذر فقال يآدم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك وعكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: Razi says many early commentators, including these authorities, adopted the literal primordial-covenant interpretation.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول قد ذهب إليه كثير من قدماء المفسرين كسعيد بن المسيب ، وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Adam saw luminous descendants, including the prophets and the especially radiant David; Adam gave David forty years of his own thousand-year lifespan, later denying the gift when death came, after which each lifespan was recorded.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أنه أبصر آدم في ذريته قوما لهم نور

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites categorically reject interpreting the verse as a literal extraction of progeny and covenant from Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: أما المعتزلة : فقد أطبقوا على أنه لا يجوز تفسير هذه الآية بهذا الوجه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their first objection says the plural phrase from their backs means God took descendants from the backs of Adam's children, never saying He took them from Adam's own back.
rows.anchor: قوله : { من بنىءادم من ظهورهم } لا شك أن قوله : { من ظهورهم }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their second objection says that if the extraction were from Adam alone, the verse would use singular back and descendants, not plural forms.
rows.anchor: أنه لو كان المرا أنه تعالى أخرج من ظهر آدم شيئا من الذرية لما قال : { من ظهورهم }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their third objection says the descendants' claim that their fathers had associated partners fits later generations, not Adam, who was not an idolater.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى حكى عن أولئك الذرية أنهم قالوا : { أو تقولوا إنما أشرك

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their fourth objection says testimony requires rationality, and a rational person could not entirely forget such a momentous event; otherwise one must equally accept reincarnation despite no memory of previous bodies.
rows.anchor: أن أخذ الميثاق لا يمكن إلا من العاقل ، فلو أخذ الله الميثاق من أولئك الذر

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that the same no-memory reasoning used to refute reincarnation also refutes a forgotten primordial covenant, making the two positions alike.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان اعتمادنا في إبطال التناسخ ليس إلا على هذا الدليل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their fifth objection is that the descendants of Adam together would occupy an immense volume that could not fit inside his small back.
rows.anchor: أن جميع الخلق الذين خلقهم الله من أولاد آدم عدد عظيم وكثرة كثيرة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their sixth objection says bodily structure is necessary for life and reason, and that all descendants with the required bodies could not fit in the earthly space, much less Adam's loins.
rows.anchor: أن البنية شرط لحصول الحياة والعقل والفهم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their seventh objection asks whether the covenant was proof at the time or later: it could not entail reward or punishment then, and forgotten testimony cannot serve as proof during earthly life.
rows.anchor: هذا الميثاق إما أن يكون قد أخذه الله منهم في ذلك الوقت ليصير حجة عليهم

rows.speaker: الكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Ka'bi argues that the descendants could not understand more than infants, who are not obligated, so they could not have been accountable at the covenant.
rows.anchor: قال الكعبي : إن حال أولئك الذرية لا يكون أعلى في الفهم والعلم من حال الأطفال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj replies that God can grant understanding to creatures such as ants and mountains, citing their speech and praise, and likewise could make the primordial descendants rational.
rows.anchor: وأجاب الزجاج عنه فقال : لما لم يبعد أن يؤتى الله النمل العقل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their ninth objection says that if the primordial descendants had full reason and ability, they were already accountable and would need a prior covenant, causing an impossible regress; if not, they could not receive the command.
rows.anchor: أن أولئك الذر في ذلك الوقت إما أن يكونوا كاملي العقول والقدر

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their tenth objection cites the statement that humans were created from a gushing fluid: if they already existed as rational beings before that fluid, the Qur'anic claim would be false.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فلينظر الإنسان مم خلق * خلق من ماء دافق }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They reject the proposed reply that God made the descendants rational and later removed their faculties, because their emergence from sperm would then be a recreation, while Muslims agree it is initial creation.
rows.anchor: قلنا : هذا باطل لأنه لو كان الأمر كذلك لما كان خلقه من النطفة خلقا على سبيل الابتداء

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Their eleventh objection first says the extracted particles must be either these same people or others; the latter option is rejected by consensus.
rows.anchor: أن تلك الذرات إما أن يقال هي عين هؤلاء الناس أو غيرهم والقول الثاني باطل بالإجماع

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: If they were the same people, they either remained conscious through sperm, embryo, and fetus, which is absurd, or did not; the latter entails four lives and three deaths, contrary to the Qur'an's two lives and two deaths.
rows.anchor: يقتضي أن يقال الإنسان حصل له الحياة أربع مرات
